articleTitle: LAAG-RV: LLM Assisted Assertion Generation for RTL Design Verification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th International Test Conference India (ITC India)
abstract: Writing SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA) is an important but complex step in verifying Register Transfer Level (RTL) designs. Conventionally, experts need to understand the design specifications and write the SVA assertions, which is time-consuming and error-prone. However, with the recent advancement of transformer models, the Large Language Models (LLMs) assisted assertion generation for design verification is gaining interest in recent times. Motivated by this, we proposed a novel LLM-based framework, LAAG-RV, to generate SVA from natural language specifications of the design. Our framework provides a one-time Verilog loop for signal synchronization in the generated SVA to improve the generated assertion quality. For our experiments, we created a custom LLM based on OpenAI GPT-4. Furthermore, we developed test cases to validate the LLM -generated assertions. Initial observations shows that some generated assertions contain issues and did not pass all the test cases. However, iteratively prompting the LLMs using carefully crafted manual prompts derived from test case failures in a simulator, the framework can generate correct SVAs. Our results on OpenTitan designs demonstrate that LLMs significantly simplify the process of generating assertions, making it efficient and less error-prone.

articleTitle: On the Asymmetry of Stuck-at Fault Sensitivity in Memristive Neural Architectures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th International Test Conference India (ITC India)
abstract: The use of memristive crossbar-based architectures has gained traction as a potential solution for performing computationally expensive tasks such as matrix-vector multiplication and vector outer product, which require significant amount of space, time, and energy. Despite being deemed inherently fault-tolerant, memristive crossbar-based neural architecture (MCNA) may often experience accuracy degradation due to hardware faults, resulting in significant variations. This study aims to comprehensively analyze the impact of stuck-at faults (SAFs) on the accuracy of a neural network during classification or regression. Contrary to the popular belief, it is observed that the impact of stuck-at-0 (SAO) and stuck-at-l (SAl) faults are highly asymmetric with respect to the loss of accuracy. Thus this study might help in planning test strategies for the enhancement of fault immunity in memristive neural architectures.

articleTitle: A Formal Based Verification Methodology for DFD Mux-Tree Hierarchies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th International Test Conference India (ITC India)
abstract: The increasing complexity of System-on-Chip (SoC) products has amplified the potential for design bugs, necessitating robust post-silicon validation to ensure system reliability. Design-for-Debug (DFD) infrastructure plays a pivotal role in providing observability to internal nodes during post-silicon debugging. However, the traditional verification of DFD's hierarchical multiplexer (mux) trees, which are essential for signal routing, is full of challenges. The legacy verification process is time-consuming, resource-intensive, and prone to human error, particularly in the manual assignment of unique identifiers (IDs) to muxes. This paper presents an innovative methodology that leverages Formal Verification and automated ID assignment to streamline the verification of SoC-level muxtrees. It replaces the laborious simulation-based approach with a more efficient formal verification process, reducing the verification time from 10 days to a single day. Additionally, the automated ID assignment algorithm ensures accuracy and consistency in the mux configuration, eliminating the risk of human error and the need for iterative manual efforts. The implementation of the proposed flow, and the significant improvements in verification efficiency demonstrated through experimental results by providing a scaled down version of the mux-tree in the case study.

articleTitle: Application of Machine Learning in De-Embedding of Signal Integrity Parameters for High Speed Serial Link
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th International Test Conference India (ITC India)
abstract: This Signal Integrity measurements are imperative to High-Speed Serial Link characterization. However, as new protocol definitions introduce higher data rates and enhanced tighter specifications, the characterization activity becomes challenging with existing equipment. For high-speed serial links, for data rates above 1 Gbps, board traces/channel affects the Signal Integrity (SI) measurements (like peak-to-peak voltage and jitter) that lead to the test failing the target specification. Therefore, de-embedding is performed to isolate the performance of the DUT (Transmitter) and eliminate the degradation due to the channel's effect. In essence, the same SI evaluation is being done twice (once on non-de-embedded signal and again on deembedded signal) that results in time overhead and increased cost of equipment and software required for the de-embedding process. In this paper, we explore the use of machine learningbased methods in de-embedding a broad class of signal integrity (SI) measurements – jitter (and all its components) and amplitude of the signal. In this paper, we talk about different ML models’ and their efficiency in predicting the de-embedded SI measurements. We discuss in detail the conventual deembedding approach and the proposed methodology. We show how the proposed method can save cost in terms of both time and money with an average error of less than 7% and timesaving of almost 25%.

articleTitle: DSP-Based Mutual Testing for Automotive and Industrial ICs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th International Test Conference India (ITC India)
abstract: In this paper, we use the idea of mutual testing to solve the problem of in-field testing. The SoC used in modern automotive and industrial electronics are complex and contain multiple instances of memories, processor cores, and analog and mixed-signal cores. Built-in Self-Test is commonly used to perform in-field testing of the ICs. In the proposed scheme, tests are applied to multiple instances of the on-chip cores and their responses are compared. If the responses are not “identical” an error is likely to be present in the SoC. We describe the use of one-dimensional Discrete Wavelet Transform for performing real-time comparison. Our technique is applicable to both digital and analog testing.

articleTitle: Accelerating First Silicon Validation By Leveraging FPGA Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th International Test Conference India (ITC India)
abstract: As technology advances, maintaining the relevance of Moore's Law in research papers leads to the development of increasingly complex chips, including heterogeneous 3D stack designs. This progression also facilitates collaborative silicon business models, allowing for the realization of multi-vendor chiplet designs. Consequently, there arises a demand for more reliable and secure validation solutions. The initial silicon bring-up is a demanding task for validators as they strive to validate all design requirements while adhering to defined timing constraints. The STIL language is widely acknowledged as the standard scripting language for post-silicon validation. This paper intro-duces a unique approach for generating test vectors from STIL scripts and evaluates its performance. The research aims to implement certain features of Automatic Test Equipment using an FPGA board and a personal computer. The implemented system was successfully utilized to perform DFT Tests such as ICL, MBIST, STUCK-AT and Transition fault models. This methodology holds potential for adoption in in-house silicon bring-up processes.

articleTitle: Concurrent Low Power Built-in Self-Test for Safety Critical SoCs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th International Test Conference India (ITC India)
abstract: In safety critical automotive devices, boot-up time and periodic checks of the correctness of logic and memory are of utmost importance for the overall operation of the device from safety perspective. Logic Built-in Self-Test (LBIST) and Memory Built-in Self-Test (MBIST) play a crucial role in ensuring the reliability and performance of safety-oriented chips. This paper first addresses the power concern of running both LBIST and MBIST parallelly and proposes novel architectures to minimize the power dissipation during LBIST and MBIST while ensuring that the target coverage is metwithin the acceptable test time. This paper then presents concurrent BIST architecture to parallelly perform LBIST and MBIST on safety islands to reduce the overall boot time which is critical to meet Automotive Safety Integrity Level (ASIL) standards.

articleTitle: Application Specific Integrated Data Processing in ADCs for High Accuracy, Low Latency Advanced Real Time Control Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th International Test Conference India (ITC India)
abstract: Advanced real time control systems re-quire low latency, high accuracy digital signal processing to address the needs of the new and emerging end equipment. Conventionally, processing is implemented in software leading to additional MIPS (Million instructions Per Second) consumption and lower accuracy. These systems also have sampling of real-world signals as one of the important steps. This is typically done using Analog-to-Digital Converters (ADCs). As accuracy and latency requirements have become more stringent, central processing of the ADC output is also becoming a bottleneck, requiring the first level of ADC processing to be brought closer to the module. This paper proposes novel techniques like sample rate modulation, accumu-lation, limit compare and post-processing to augment conventional ADC processing, improving accuracy and reducing latency. In addition to the control processing demands, functional safety requirements are also increasing. Functional safety diagnostic logic deployed in hardware offers the additional benefits of lower la-tency (thus impacting the Fault-Tolerant Time Interval (FTTI)) and lower deployment effort. The techniques proposed in this paper helped to reduce MIPS by up to 15%, enabled up to 15 times faster fault detection and provided effective number of bits (ENOB) gain of up to 2 bits. The safety checker logic implemented in this system helped achieve system-level ASIL-D with much smaller software overhead compared to conventional systems.

articleTitle: Shift Power Reduction in High-Performance Clock Network Designs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th International Test Conference India (ITC India)
abstract: With the rapid development of deep submicron (DSM) high-performance VLSI circuits, building a robust clock tree with minimal insertion delays, skews and jitter has turned out to be challenging. Several techniques have been developed to reduce the clock insertion delay & clock skew. A few such techniques are Clock Mesh CTS, Multi Source CTS or Multi Entry CTS. These techniques help reduce insertion delays, skews and jitter across the design but can adversely affect the power since the significant section of a design driven by a clock source can toggle within a short time. Impact will be higher during the scan shift phase where all clock gating circuits are transparent in blocks targeted for ATPG. Due to a significant reduction in insertion delay and clock skew, the clock edge reaches all the sinks in design quickly resulting in a significant amount of activity happening in a short span of every shift clock edge. In this paper, we discuss the adverse effects of high-performance clock network schemes on Shift power and techniques to save Shift power in such scenarios. Results from the analysis of a few blocks will also be shared. Solution described in this paper is applicable in high performance designs where clock mesh clock tree network architectures are implemented.

articleTitle: Optimize Test Pattern Count via Efficient Operation of IEEE 1687 SIBs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th International Test Conference India (ITC India)
abstract: This paper discusses an approach to operate on a network of IEEE 1687 Segment Insertion Bits (SIBs) such that multiple Intellectual Property (IP) blocks in an Application Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) System on Chip (SoC), each being controlled by an embedded network of SIBs can be accessed simultaneously. With this approach multiple IP blocks can be tested together in a single test cycle, thereby reducing the total test time and test data volume thus impacting the test cost positively. IEEE 1687 standard is widely used in the industry and by operating on an IJTAG network of SIBs efficiently, an EDA tool, can generate an efficient set of test patterns. This paper also discusses the various design topologies that exist with the usage of SIBs and the challenges that an EDA tool faces while operating on a network of multiple SIBs.

articleTitle: Optimized Timing Aware ATPG for At-Speed Test of Cell Internal Faults
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th International Test Conference India (ITC India)
abstract: Achieving high structural defect coverage is extremely critical to achieve low defective parts per million (DPPM) and to eliminate the need for additional system level tests. New defect oriented test methods such as cell-aware tests (CAT) have been introduced to improve test quality on advanced technology nodes. In general, addition of new fault models bring in challenges with regard to test cost impact and execution turn-around for large design scales and complexities. In this paper, we specifically focus on the issue of pattern count and runtime issues introduced by the need for timing aware automatic test pattern generation (ATPG) for testing cell-internal small-delay defects. We present novel strategies and CAT test generation methodologies to shrink the size of the fault list for timing aware ATPG (TA-ATPG) to target only the critical and relevant cell-internal small-delay faults. The experimental results by using the proposed methods on a large-scale design are shared to highlight the efficacy of the proposed solution in terms of runtime reduction and test efficiency improvement.

articleTitle: Exploring Cross-Temperature Reliability in 3D NAND Through Layer-Dependent Bit Error Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th International Test Conference India (ITC India)
abstract: We conduct experimental investigation of cross- temperature reliability concern of data stored in a commercial 64-layer 3D NAND floating-gate (FG) flash memory chip through characterization of error bits at different layers of TLC pages.

articleTitle: In-Field Fault Detection Framework for Edge Accelerator Using Autoencoder
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th International Test Conference India (ITC India)
abstract: AI accelerators are ubiquitous across all computational domains, including safety-critical systems such as autonomous driving. However, they are also susceptible to dynamic faults due to aging-related and missed permanent manufacturing defects manifesting during in-field operation. Detecting such faults early during in-field operations is essential, particularly for the processing elements with fewer resources. The fault detection framework should operate at the level of predictions rather than individual neurons to achieve fault detection with minimal resource overhead. The output of the classifier network could have captured the fault effects as they propagate through both hardware and software architecture. In this work, we propose a methodology that uses the input image and the logits (output of the classifier network without softmax function) to predict the correctness of the prediction. The method detects the faults that significantly reduce the topl accuracy by more than 50%. This methodology necessitates one-time training of the decoder and additional computation of 1904 neurons using a 3-layer lightweight detection network during in-field operation for fault detection. However, traditional redundancy-based methods such as Dual Modular Redundancy require an additional 4950 neuron computation, equivalent to the classifier network. The proposed method results in around 61 % lesser neuron computation compared to traditional methods and a 99.99 % critical fault detection rate.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Test Point Insertion Strategy for Improved Test Metrics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th International Test Conference India (ITC India)
abstract: Rapid increase in design complexity and new defects in shrinking technology nodes have led to development of advanced fault models like cell-aware, small delay defects., etc., resulting in an increase of cumulative patterns required for screening the devices to achieve higher coverage targets. However, there is a growing need to reduce the cost of testing. The fine balance between improved test coverage and reduced pattern count has been traditionally addressed with test point insertion, but with an incurred area penalty. In this paper we will discuss a hybrid test point insertion technique which addresses the requirements of coverage, pattern volume and area.

articleTitle: Test Selection for Periodic In-field health-check monitoring in fail-safe applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th International Test Conference India (ITC India)
abstract: Systems on chip used in automotive and industrial applications continue to grow in complexity, with many em-bedded processors, memories, and peripheral controllers. Since functional safety of ICs used in these applications is important, periodic in-field testing of the embedded blocks is a necessity. There is a huge number of possibilities for testing the embedded components, such as hardware-enabled BIST, software-enabled BIST, and mutual testing to name a few. In this paper, we consider the problem of selecting an optimal subset of these unit test cases and model it a graph-theoretical optimization problem. We consider the energy dissipation of the test algorithms and the run-time of the test algorithms as two important considerations in the optimization. We propose an exhaustive algorithm as well as a greedy optimization algorithm for the test selection problem.

articleTitle: Silicon Correlation in SLM: An Integrated Strategy for Chip Performance Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th International Test Conference India (ITC India)
abstract: Ever increasing complexities and performance requirements of chips necessitates paradigm shift from our traditional approaches. This translates into the need for continuous monitoring and optimization though out the life cycle of the chip. Silicon life cycle management coupled with silicon correlation offers an innovative solution for this challenge. Silicon correlation in SLM (Silicon Lifecycle Management) serves as strategic tool to ensure the predictive fidelity of design models while bridging gap between pre-silicon models and post-silicon realities. The holistic approach enables consistent prediction of device performance, reliability anomalies and process variations. This paper outlines an integrated strategy that enhances chip performance by utilizing data from pre- and post- silicon phases, perform correlation, delve into the challenges associated with flow and methodology of integrating SLM IPs into the design process. Using a case study, we discuss the data extraction techniques and the analysis of gap-to-target silicon data to demonstrate practical applications of our strategy. In essence, silicon correlation gives actional insights into chip health, enabling more precise decision-making to meet performance targets.

articleTitle: An FPGA Based Emulation of Source Synchronous Protocol-Aware Timing Stress Test
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th International Test Conference India (ITC India)

authors.preferredName: P R R K Tirumalesu Manda

abstract: This paper discusses about an FPGA based emulation of source synchronous protocol-aware hardware which can be used to test the timing parameters of various medium speed protocols on silicon. Due to the multi-instance and multi-site test capability of the proposed method, the test time of SPI timing parameters reduces by more than 15 times. It creates testability for erstwhile untestable timing parameters of SDHC and eMMC protocols.

articleTitle: Shift-Left Principle for Faster Post-Silicon Validation: LPDDR4 Controller Bring-Up
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 8th International Test Conference India (ITC India)
abstract: The increasing demand for high-performance memory solutions in autonomous automotive systems has led to the widespread adoption of high-speed interfaces, such as, Low Power Double Data Rate 4 (LPDDR4) interfaces. The post- silicon validation (PSV) of LPDDR4 interface is a time- consuming and resource-intensive process and becomes the critical path for release to end-customer. This paper proposes a methodology to reduce the time and effort of PSV of a System- on-Chip with LPDDR4 memory controller by adopting the shift- left principle. PCB simulations and firmware verification were shifted left to pre-silicon phase and is performed in parallel with the SoC design. It is shown that 22% of effort is shifted from post-silicon to pre-silicon phase and another 15% effort is eliminated, thereby shortening the time to market by 37%.
